from math import gcd


def best_average(a: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
    n = len(a)
    prefix = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i, x in enumerate(a):
        prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + x

    # Start from the whole array as the candidate average p/q.
    p, q = prefix[n], n

    # Dinkelbach iteration: find a subarray of length >= k whose average
    # exceeds p/q, i.e. maximize q*sum - p*len. Stop when none exists.
    while True:
        min_val = None
        min_idx = -1
        best = 0
        best_i = best_j = -1
        for j in range(k, n + 1):
            i = j - k
            # Keep the smallest q*P[i] - p*i among valid starts i <= j - k.
            cur = q * prefix[i] - p * i
            if min_val is None or cur < min_val:
                min_val = cur
                min_idx = i
            val = (q * prefix[j] - p * j) - min_val
            if val > best:
                best = val
                best_i = min_idx
                best_j = j
        if best <= 0:
            break
        p = prefix[best_j] - prefix[best_i]
        q = best_j - best_i

    g = gcd(p, q)
    return [p // g, q // g]
